description:
Continue the conversation in an interactive message. Partially evaluate roughly the next three useful turns: use what is already known to explain the situation, offer consequential proposals, and prepare the follow-ups each plausible answer would invite. Start with a small decision surface and a grounded contribution; put further useful analysis or proposals inside the relevant branch. Do not repeat a summary as an editable input unless editing it changes the next action. An investigation or an editable proposal is a successful outcome; stop when the next step needs new evidence rather than inventing that evidence or extending an exhaustive questionnaire.

Separate observations from assumptions. Ground recommendations in the conversation or inspected material; mark unknowns and make proposed wording/plans editable with input defaults. Use markdown/text for substantive analysis, select for mutually exclusive directions and multi for compatible approaches the user may explore together. Put answer-specific continuations under exact option-text keys; each selected multi branch stays visible alongside the others. Prefer reveals for checked or selection-wide continuations, then when for cross-branch interactions. Roughly three turns is a foresight horizon, not a required depth. Inspect repository facts yourself; ask the user about consequential choices, not facts you can retrieve. Defaults are proposals until Submit.

FAILURE CASE: a topic selector followed by "Tell me more" delegates the thinking back to the user. Contribute a hypothesis, tradeoff or proposal at the selected branch instead; when evidence is missing, offer the next investigation.

WORKED EXAMPLE: the following CI timings are fictional supplied evidence, not facts about your repository. Notice the analysis, simultaneously explorable changes, editable plans, uncertainty leading to investigation, and joint benchmark proposal. Transfer that structure rather than copying its assumptions:

Classic widgets: text, markdown, slider, check, input (default/placeholder/rows), select, multi, rank (partial priority order), group and linear page. title is optional; omit redundant headings. Give options decision-relevant descriptions (because is an alias). multi.default accepts an option string or array. Exact option keys hold follow-up arrays; reveals appears while checked or once a selection exists. Conditions use bare ids, selected(id, value), count(id), any/all, comparisons, && || ! and parentheses; quote values containing a closing parenthesis. Hidden values read as unset even with defaults. References must exist; cycles including ancestor/descendant dependencies are rejected. If pages are needed, every top-level element is a page with Back/Next and one final Submit; page.when can skip steps.

Keep notes enabled. Every select/multi supplies Other (please specify) with free text automatically. Notes and unexpected answers can change the problem representation; explicit corrections override conflicting widgets. Ask only what still blocks progress. Use unique ASCII ids; avoid status, button, error, _notes, _labels, _route, __proto__, constructor, prototype and generated <id>_other_text collisions. Option values cannot collide with widget properties. Repair path-specific validation errors and retry. No page.next, conversation nodes, semantic routing, after_submit or intermediate submission exists.

Opening the tool returns awaiting_input with formId and definition, not a decision. Wait for the user message {"type":"popup_result","formId":"…","submissionId":"…","result":{…}}. Its terminal classic result is {"status":"completed","button":"submit","<id>":<value>,"_labels":{…},"_notes":"…"} or {"status":"cancelled"}. A repeated submissionId is duplicate delivery: do not repeat the action. Cancellation stops this question; do not reopen automatically. There is no backend answer storage.

Interpret the submitted evidence: absent keys were hidden or on unvisited pages; input "" is blank, select null unchosen, multi/rank [] empty, check false unchecked. Select returns option text; multi/rank return arrays (rank in priority order); slider returns a number; Other adds <id>_other_text. _labels explains ids and _notes adds instructions. Resume the original task from the actual answer, including corrections, without mistaking the opening acknowledgment or an unsubmitted default for agreement.
